events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
FFWEPZ

The National Weather Service in El Paso Tx/Santa Teresa has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
East Central Grant County in southwestern New Mexico...
Northwestern Luna County in southwestern New Mexico...

* Until 945 AM MDT.

* At 646 AM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 0.5 and 1 inch of rain
has fallen. Additional rainfall amounts up to 1 inch are possible
in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Faywood and Butterfield Trail Estates.

events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
SMWMFL

The National Weather Service in Miami has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Coastal waters from Chokoloskee to Bonita Beach FL out 20 NM...
Coastal waters from East Cape Sable to Chokoloskee FL out 20 NM...

* Until 915 AM EDT.

* At 838 AM EDT, a severe thunderstorm capable of producing
waterspouts was located near Cape Romano, or 11 nm south of Marco
Island, moving east at 10 knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can easily overturn boats and create locally
hazardous seas. Small craft could be damaged in briefly
higher winds and suddenly higher waves.

* Locations impacted include...
Chokoloskee, Cape Romano Aquatic Preserve, Cape Romano, and Marco
Island.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHEN...Until 800 AM MDT.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, slot canyons,
normally dry washes and other low-lying and flood-prone locations
is imminent or occurring. Waterways continue to rise due to excess
runoff from earlier rainfall.

earlier thunderstorms.

Escalante, Boulder, the Escalante River drainage from the
headwaters to Powell, Last Chance, Croton Creek, Dry Rock Creek,
Coyote Gulch and all slot canyons in the Escalante Drainage and
near Hole-in-the-Rock Road.
